newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Kabila, Mobutu agree to Zaire talks Wednesday - UN.
newsitem.headline: Kabila, Mobutu agree to Zaire talks Wednesday - UN.

text.p: Zaire's beleaguered president Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila have both agreed to U.N.-sponsored talks aboard a South African navy vessel on Wednesday, senior U.N. sources said.
But the sources said on Friday they had no firm guarantees from either side that the meeting would go ahead as planned.
"We made an appointment with both of them. But we have no guarantees," the source said.

Earlier on Friday one of Kabila's inisters in the southeastern city of Lumumbashi confirmed the venue for the talks would be a South African navy ship, as in the first meeting of the two foes on Sunday.
The U.N. source said South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who arrived in Lubumbashi on Friday, would see Kabila to "try to get him move towards a more conciliatory position".
Mbeki's trip is part of a South African attempt to mediate a peaceful transition of power in Zaire.
Kabila's rebels now control three quarters of the country and Mobutu has agreed in principle to step down after more than 30 years in power.

Senior U.N. sources who asked not to be named said the French government, a key supporter of Mobutu, had said the Zairean ruler could live in exile in France, where he owns a luxury villa on the Riviera, if and when he leaves his country.
The French Foreign Ministry said this week that the question was "not topical".
But a senior U.N. source said: "The French have said they will take Mobutu."
